newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol airport tigthens noise regulations.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol airport tigthens noise regulations.

text.p: Amsterdam Schiphol airport will tighten its regulations concerning the older and nosier Chapter-2 aircraft from November one, the airport authority stated in a letter to the carriers.
The major aim of the stricter rules is to reduce the number of Chapter-2 flights, the airport said in a statement.
In 1996, ten percent of Schiphol's traffic are Chapter-2 flights down from 14 percent in 1995. Next year, the airport authority aims to reduce the number of these flights to less than seven percent.

Under the new rules, Chapter-2 aircraft face a total night ban. Freight aircraft including Boeing 707s and DC-8s will now be unable to arrive or take-off during the night and passenger aircraft such as the BAC 1-11, Boeing 727, 737-100, 737-200, DC-9 and Fokker 28 will also be banned.
Even though the Ilyushin 76 and Tupolev 154M are not classed as Chapter-2 aircraft, they will also be effected by the new regulations, the Schiphol authority stated.

Schiphol is also increasing its charges for these aircraft by 100 percent. Aircraft with a payload of up to 100 tonnes will now be charged an additional 600 guilders and those with a payload of over 100 tonnes will pay 900 guilders extra if the payload is above 100 tons.

For instance a Chapter-2 737-200 loaded with less than 100 tons now will have to pay a 1,600 guilders landing fee and the more heavily charged 707 freighter with more than 100 tons payload will pay a 2,700 guilders landing fee.

Carriers can get some money back but they have to sign a contract with Schiphol airport stating that they will soon renew their fleet and eventually phase out their Chapter-2 aircraft, the airport authority stated.

Schiphol is also no longer allowing any new Chapter-2 aircraft operators into the airport and from April one, 1997, 747-100 aircraft with JT9D-7 engines will also be hit by these new stricter rules. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
